paper_title: Stellar cooling bounds on new light particles: plasma mixing effects
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter epsilon (dimensionless), as plotted on y-axis
notes: Hardy & Lasenby (1611.05852) present updated stellar/SN cooling bounds including plasma mixing effects. The headline new dark-photon result is the SN1987A energy-loss bound (Figure 3, epsilon vs m from ~0.1 MeV to ~1 GeV). No numerical table is provided; the data_points are approximate values of the lower exclusion boundary reconstructed from the described scaling (epsilon ~ 1/m below the SN plasma frequency ~20 MeV, minimum epsilon ~ few x 1e-11 near resonance, steep weakening above ~100 MeV from Boltzmann/decay effects) and from the widely used digitized version of Fig. 3. Upper boundary of exclusion (trapping/decay) is not included. This is a stellar/SN bound, NOT a DM haloscope, so no local DM density is assumed. The paper also derives bounds on B-L vectors (g_BL vs mass) and scalars coupling to electrons/nucleons (alpha_phi-ee < 4e-32 from RG resonant production, alpha_phi-NN < 1e-25) and Higgs-portal mixing sin(theta) < 3e-10 for m < 2 keV; only the dark photon result is encoded here per the coupling_type hint.
